How it works

  1. Add a layer. Paste the service URL (for example .../FeatureServer/0 or .../wfs). For a WFS service you choose which feature types to load.
  2. Check the data. The layer appears on the map, with its geometry type, coordinate system and attribute table available before you export.
  3. Export. The tool requests the layer’s object IDs, downloads the features in small pages of 200, and converts them in your browser to GeoPackage, Shapefile, GeoJSON, CSV, KML or GPX.

Coordinates are exported in WGS84 (longitude/latitude) for ArcGIS layers, and WFS layers keep the coordinate system the server reports. Attribute values are exported as the server returns them. For a deeper explanation, read our guide to coordinate systems and projections.

Frequently asked questions

Is Geo Server Data Downloader free?

Yes. There is no account, no sign-up and no export fee. Some blog articles may show ads, which help cover hosting.

Which formats can I export?

GeoPackage, Shapefile (zipped), GeoJSON, CSV, KML and GPX. Conversion runs in your browser using GDAL compiled to WebAssembly.

Is there a limit on how many features I can download?

The tool does not impose a feature cap and ignores the 1,000-record limit that many ArcGIS services apply to a single request. It downloads every object ID the layer reports, so very large layers are limited only by your browser’s memory.

Does it support WFS?

Yes, for WFS 1.0.0 to 2.0.0 servers that can return GeoJSON and allow cross-origin browser requests. WMS is not supported because it serves map images, not feature data.

Why do some ArcGIS downloads fail with "Failed to execute query"?

Servers differ in what they accept. Many reject requests for server-built GeoJSON or very long ID lists. This tool asks for plain JSON in small pages of 200 object IDs and converts it to GeoJSON in your browser, which works on a wider range of servers.

Is my data uploaded to your servers?

No. The site has no backend. Your browser requests features directly from the data provider and converts them locally.
